[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Shared VPC service-project association is created without waiting for the configured project APIs to finish enabling. In particular, the Compute Engine API must be available for the service project before it is associated; the sibling host-project resource already waits for project_services.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Shared VPC service-project attachment uses the Compute API but has no ordering edge to the project service enablement. Enablement must complete before creating this association; add an explicit dependency on the project services.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Shared VPC service-project association uses Compute Engine functionality but has no ordering edge to project_services. When compute.googleapis.com is enabled by this module, association can race API activation.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service` attaches this project to a Shared VPC host, which requires the Compute Engine API to already be enabled in the service project. Nothing establishes that ordering: `host_project` comes from `var.shared_vpc_service_config` and `service_project` from `local.project.project_id`, and there is no `depends_on`, so this resource can be applied before `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` finishes activating compute.googleapis.com and fail with an API-disabled error. Its counterpart `:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host` already declares exactly this ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project via the Compute API, but unlike its host-side counterpart (:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host) it has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services, so the attachment can be attempted before compute.googleapis.com is enabled in the service project.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project via the Compute API, but unlike google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host (which depends_on project_services) it has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services, so it may run before compute.googleapis.com is enabled.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project of an external host; the Compute API must be enabled in this (service) project before the association succeeds. :resource.google_project_service.project_services performs the API activation, and the sibling resources google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host and google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots already depend on it, but this resource has no dependency on it and can be applied before the Compute API is active.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels creates channels through the Cloud Monitoring API but has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services. When monitoring.googleapis.com is being enabled by this same module, the channel create call can race API enablement (which is eventually consistent) and fail. Its downstream sibling google_monitoring_alert_policy depends on these channels, so the failure propagates. Add depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services].

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels` creates Cloud Monitoring notification channels but does not wait for `google_project_service.project_services`. When `monitoring.googleapis.com` is enabled via this module, channels can be created before the API is active. No attribute reference expresses this ordering; a bare depends_on is appropriate.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels uses the Cloud Monitoring API (via `project = local.project.project_id`), but the graph shows no dependency (implicit or explicit) on :resource.google_project_service.project_services. Monitoring is not enabled by default on new projects; if this module is enabling `monitoring.googleapis.com` in the same apply, channel creation can run before the API is active and fail. The module already uses an explicit depends_on on project_services for every other API-dependent resource (e.g. google_compute_project_metadata_item.default, google_logging_project_sink.sink, google_cloud_quotas_quota_preference.default); this resource is missing it.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels calls the Cloud Monitoring API against `local.project.project_id`, but has no ordering relationship with :resource.google_project_service.project_services. Sibling observability resources in this module (e.g. logging sinks, quota preferences) already depend on project_services for exactly this reason; without it, channels can be applied before monitoring.googleapis.com is activated and fail with an API-not-enabled error.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels creates notification channels via the Cloud Monitoring API, which is not enabled by default; if monitoring.googleapis.com is being activated by :resource.google_project_service.project_services in the same apply, channel creation races the API activation and fails. Every other API-dependent resource in this module (quotas, compute metadata, sinks, service identities) declares depends_on on :resource.google_project_service.project_services, but this one does not.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_alert_policy.alerts is created via the Cloud Monitoring API but only references notification channels implicitly; it never waits for :resource.google_project_service.project_services, so alert policies can fail when monitoring.googleapis.com is enabled in the same apply.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_monitoring_alert_policy.alerts` creates alert policies against the Cloud Monitoring API but has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`. When `monitoring.googleapis.com` is enabled by this module, policy creation can race API activation. This is not expressible as a data reference, so an explicit depends_on is the fix.

:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary registers the project in a metrics scope through the Monitoring API but has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services, so it can be attempted before monitoring.googleapis.com is enabled.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary` registers this project into a Metrics Scope using the Cloud Monitoring API, but never waits for `google_project_service.project_services`. With `monitoring.googleapis.com` enabled by this module, registration can occur before the API is active on the project. No attribute reference captures this ordering, so a bare depends_on is the appropriate fix.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary registers this project in metrics scopes through the Cloud Monitoring API, but the graph shows no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services. The monitoring API is not enabled by default, so when this module provisions `monitoring.googleapis.com` in the same apply the monitored-project registration may execute before the API is usable. Like the other API-dependent resources in this module, it needs an explicit ordering on :resource.google_project_service.project_services.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary uses the Cloud Monitoring API but has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services; the monitoring API must be activated in the project before monitored projects can be registered.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary registers this project under a metrics scope using the Monitoring API (locations.global.metricsScopes.projects), which requires monitoring.googleapis.com to be enabled in this project. The API activation is performed by :resource.google_project_service.project_services, but this resource does not depend on it, so the two can race on a fresh project.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_logging_metric.metrics writes log-based metrics through the Cloud Logging API but never depends on :resource.google_project_service.project_services. The sibling google_logging_project_sink.sink in the same module does declare that dependency, so this resource can still race logging.googleapis.com enablement and fail with a 403/SERVICE_DISABLED error.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_logging_metric.metrics` creates logs-based metrics against the Logging API, but has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`. In a project where `logging.googleapis.com` is enabled by this module, the metric can be attempted before the API is active and fail. The sibling sink resource does model this ordering; the metric should too (no clean attribute reference exists, so a bare depends_on is appropriate).
